## Local Typecheck Results (following egdev6's suggestion)

Ran `bun typecheck` from `packages/opencode` locally. Found **4 type errors** introduced by this PR -- all related to Zod/Effect Schema incompatibility after the recent migration:

### Error 1 -- `src/tool/terminal.ts:213`
```
Argument of type 'Effect<<{ description: string; parameters: ZodPipe<ZodTransform, ZodDiscriminatedUnion>; ... >>' 
  is not assignable to parameter of type 'Effect<Init<Decoder, ...>>'
```
**Root cause:** `Tool.define` now expects Effect `Decoder` (after Effect Schema migration), but the PR still passes a `ZodDiscriminatedUnion`.

### Error 2 -- `src/tool/terminal.ts:664`
```
Type 'ZodPipe<ZodTransform, ZodDiscriminatedUnion<[...], "action">>' 
  is missing properties from 'Decoder': "Rebuild", Iso, [TypeId], "ast", ...
```
**Same root cause** -- the discriminated union schema needs migration to Effect Schema.

### Error 3 & 4 -- `test/session/prompt.test.ts:204` and `snapshot-tool-race.test.ts:158`
```
Type 'Layer<..., ServeError, Service>' is not assignable to 'Layer<..., ServeError, never>'
```

### Error 5 -- `test/tool/terminal.test.ts:240`
```
This expression is not callable. Type '{ effect: { ...} }' has no call signatures.
```

### Summary
These are real type errors. The branch needs Zod schemas migrated to Effect Schema to be compatible with the current `dev` branch. Happy to address this if helpful.

## Update: Root cause is self-kill, not just mouse events

After further investigation with OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1 set, the crash still happens. The real root cause is that opencode itself runs as a node process.

When opencode executes the following command (as shown in the TUI):

\\\powershell
Stop-Process -Name node -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
\\\

This kills ALL node processes on the system — including opencode itself. It is a self-kill.

The \shell.ts killTree()\ function on Windows uses \	askkill /pid <PID> /f /t\ which correctly targets a specific process tree. But when the tool execution path runs \Stop-Process -Name node -Force\, it is untargeted and kills every node process by name.

### Suggested Fix

The kill command should exclude the current process PID. For example:

\\\powershell
# Instead of:
Stop-Process -Name node -Force

# Use:
Get-Process -Name node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { .Id -ne 47540 } | Stop-Process -Force
\\\

Or better yet, use \	askkill /pid <specific-pid>\ to only target the specific child process tree, rather than killing all node processes by name.

@github-actions: Opencode Desktop is the reverse: they want to ssh into a machine and use that as the AI model connection. This proposes an abritrary linux shell running opencode, then connecting to remote systems that have zero AI infrastructure and you don't want to install anything. You want to maintain those systems via open code.

Websocket is a transport protocol to operate the UI or the TUI. Websocket could be a protocol layer, such as someone builds a Dockerfile that connectable via Websocket and provides their own shell out. That's what something like this does: https://github.com/superfly/flyssh and could be similar.
